sentences.text: This is first application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973 for grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant who has been arrested relating to FIR/Crime No.181/2023 dated 17.06.2023 registered at Police Station Devendra Nagar, District Panna, for an offence punishable under Sections 376 and 376(2)(n) of IPC, Sections 3/4 and 5L/6 of POCSO Act and Sections 3(1)(w)(ii) and 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 21.06.2023 and the trial will take considerable time to conclude.
sentences._hearing_file: Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: He further submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
sentences._hearing_file: Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: The applicant is a permanent resident of district and is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

sentences.text: According to the documents available in the case diary, there is a birth certificate placed therein which discloses the date of birth to be 13.08.2006 but the name of prosecutrix is not mentioned therein.

sentences.text:
On that basis,
it can be inferred that on the date of FIR, she had completed the age of 18 years.
sentences._hearing_file: Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023.json

sentences.text:
According to her,
she has sexual relationship with applicant first time in the month of October, 2022, thus, she was more than 17 years when this physical relationship was established.
sentences._hearing_file: Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is revealed in the FIR that she was threatened that her photographs be made viral on Instagram by applicant, if she refuses to physical relation but it is not disclosed in the case diary when and how these photographs were taken by the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: The charge-sheet does not disclose that the seizure of mobile phone of applicant for collection of evidence regarding photographs available therein.
sentences._hearing_file: Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023.json

sentences.text:
It was claimed by the prosecutrix in her statements recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. that applicant had made her photographs viral on Instagram but later her statements were recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. in denial to that fact.
Having considered the unstable nature of allegation made against the applicant and also in the light of the fact that his mobile phone was not seized during investigation, this Court deems it fit to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Vimal Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023.json

sentences.text:
It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.

On 29.07.2020 at about 10:30 a.m., the prosecutrix sought a lift from a motorcyclist near Dubhiya Turn.

On the following day,
the appellant allegedly met her outside the school premises, spoke to her and obtained her mobile NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18125 3 CRA-316-2026 number.
Thereafter, the appellant and the prosecutrix remained in telephonic contact.
It is further alleged that approximately one year prior to the lodging of the FIR, the appellant invited the prosecutrix to Gunaur, where she went and engaged in physical relations with him at about 1:00 p.m. in a rented room belonging to his friend.
On the basis of the said complaint, a case was registered at Crime No. 181/2023 under Sections 376 and 376(2)(N)
of the IPC, Sections 3/4 and 5L/6 of the POCSO Act, and Sections 3(1)(W)(ii) and 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act at Police Station Devendranagar.

It is a settled principle of criminal NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

In the present case,

It is further submitted that there was unexplained and inordinate delay in lodging the FIR.
The alleged incidents are stated to have occurred over a prolonged period; however, the complaint was lodged after considerable delay without any satisfactory explanation.
There is no independent corroboration of the allegations.
